dataset.name: Biogeochemistry of Pond B (Savannah River Site, South Carolina, USA): Water column and Sediments
description: Pond B at Savannah River Site (SRS, South Carolina) is a monomictic reservoir that received SRS R reactor cooling water from 1961–1964. Previous studies conducted between the 1980s–1990s on the water column and sediments of Pond B measured trace amounts of Pu (33 MBq 238Pu and 430 MBq 239,240Pu), 241Am, and 137Cs. Since then, the pond has been relatively isolated and the radionuclide concentrations have not been monitored over time. Herein, about 30 years after the last publication on Pond B, we are re-evaluating the geochemistry and radionuclide distribution within Pond B at five locations along a horizontal transect from the inlet to outlet. In addition, we are conducting the first analysis of the microbial community composition. This data package consists of water column measurements (1) using a multi-probe sonde, (2) plutonium isotopes and total concentrations, (3) total organic/inorganic carbon concentrations, (4) trace metals and major ions concentrations, and (6) microbial community composition. Sediment measurements include (1) plutonium isotopes and total concentrations and (2) microbial community composition.
For sediment core and porewater, please see other Pond B data package (ess-dive-60d2352a4495472-20200615T203925174).
The data in this package will be submitted for peer review in 2023.

Water column profiling collection
At each location, the water column was profiled using two multi-probe sondes (Aqua TROLL 600 vented and nonvented; In-Situ, Inc., USA) connected via a rugged cable splitter. Each sonde was configured with four probes, and in addition to on-board detectors, several parameters were measured every few seconds by the two sondes, including depth, pH, ORP, temperature, conductivity, ammonium, nitrate, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll a, phycocyanin, salinity, and turbidity. All parameters were calibrated before each field sampling campaign following the manufacturer’s protocols. After profiling the water column, water samples were collected by pumping water to the surface through tubing (Masterflex C-Flex ULTRA tubing L/S 18, Cat. No.: EW-06434-18, Cole-Parmer, USA) connected in parallel to the sonde cable with zip-ties. A field pump (Pump Quick Release Water Sampler, Cat. No.: CJ0500, Global Water, USA) connected to a battery (Cat. No.: 00-010, Global Water, USA) was used to continuously pump water. Water was allowed to pump for approximately 5 min before sampling and the tubing was covered by tarp to prevent photoreactions. The approximate flowrate (300–500 mL/min) was measured by filling a 50 mL falcon tube.
Microbial cell counts were determined by aseptically filling a 50 mL falcon tube, which was subsequently stored at 4ºC (formaldehyde added to a final concentration of 3% within 24 hours). Total inorganic and organic carbon (TIC/TOC) was measured on water samples filtered through a 0.22 µm Sterivex filter (Cat. No.: SVGVL10RC, MilliporeSigma, USA) and collected into amber Type I borosilicate glass vials (TraceClean® 40 mL processed vials, open top; Cat. No.: 89093-870, VWR, USA). The vials were stored at 4ºC. Once the filter clogged (≤ 120 mL water filtered), the filter was disconnected, and water was removed from the filter with 30 mL air before immediately placing the Sterivex into black, sterile Whirl-Pak® bags (Cat. No.: B01418, Enasco, USA) onto dry ice for microbial community analysis (DNA extraction). An air control was also prepared by filtering air through a 0.22 µm Sterivex for about 15 min. For gamma counting, plutonium concentrations, and trace metals and major ions concentrations, water was pumped directly into HDPE bottles (certified clean; Cat. No.: 319-1000 and 319-0125, ThermoFisher Scientific, USA). All HDPE bottles were filled to the top and stored at 4ºC.

Gamma counting and radionuclide concentrations (MC-ICP-MS)
The LLNL standard operating procedure for plutonium (SOP-UGTA-135, LLNL-TM-743587) was followed.

Total organic/inorganic carbon concentrations
The LLNL standard operating procedure for total organic/inorganic concentrations (SOP-UGTA-116, LLNL-TM-743469) was followed using a TOC/TIC analyzer (Shimadzu).

Trace metals and major anions concentrations
Water for trace metals and major anions was filtered through 0.45 µm PTFE filter (Acrodisc CR PTFE; Cat. No. 4219T) into a trace-metal free 50 mL falcon tube. For trace metals, 1% HNO3 was added to the filtered pond water. Three process blanks were made using Milli-Q water. Samples were stored at 4ºC until measurement following the LLNL standard operating procedure for trace metals (SOP-UGTA-134, LLNL-TM-743586) and major anions (SOP-UGTA-120, LLNL-TM-743538).

Microbial community composition (DNA extraction, sequencing, and analysis)
DNA was extracted using the DNeasy PowerBiofilm Kit (Cat. No.: 24000-50, Qiagen, Germany). The 0.22 µm Sterivex filters (Cat. No.: SVGVL10RC, MilliporeSigma, MA, USA) were first thawed on ice and aseptically opened inside a biosafety cabinet using a sterilized pipe cutter. The filter was removed and placed inside a PowerBiofilm bead tube. Subsequently, the manufacturer’s protocol was used to obtain DNA. The DNA quality and quantity were determined by NanoDrop 2000c (ThermoFisher Scientific, USA) and Qubit Fluorometer 2.0 (ThermoFisher Scientific, USA), respectively. The Qubit dsDNA high sensitivity assay kit (Cat. No.: Q32854, ThermoFisher Scientific, USA) was used to quantify the DNA. The DNA was stored at -20ºC until sequencing.
Samples were shipped to the Molecular Research DNA Lab (MRDNA) for 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Briefly, the V4 variable region (primers 515/806) was amplified using the HotStarTaq Plus Master Mix Kit (Qiagen) for 30-35 cycles. PCR products were purified using Ampure XP beads and were pooled to prepare an Illumina DNA library following the manufacturer’s guidelines for MiSeq.
The raw sequencing data was then demultiplexed using Qiime and the R package Dada2 v1.12.1 was used to filter and trim the reads with options: truncLen = c(220,220), trimLeft = c(8,8), maxN = 0, maxEE = c(2,5), truncQ = 2, rm.phix = TRUE. The error rates were estimated and sequences dereplicated before inferring amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). Subsequently, the forward and reverse reads were merged, followed by the removal of chimeras. Taxonomy was assigned to the species level using the SILVA v132 database. The R package Decontam v1.4.0 was then used to remove contaminant sequences found in the DNA Extraction Control and Field Sampling Air Control. The R package Phyloseq v1.24.2 was used to define the prevalence threshold of each taxa and all taxa below the prevalence threshold were removed. Afterwards, the R package MetagenomeSeq v1.26.3 was used to normalize the reads amongst the samples by following the cumulative-sum scaling approach. Phyloseq was then used to examine the relationship between the microbial community composition and the geochemistry of Pond B.

Cell Counts
An aliquot of the sample (0.5 mL or 1 mL) was then stained with 5% (v/v) of a 1:100 dilution of SYBR(TM) Gold Nucleic Acid Gel Stain (Cat. No.: S11494, Invitrogen) for at least 30 min at 4ºC. Subsequently, the sample was filtered through a 0.22 um filter (Nucleopore polycarbonate black membrane filter 25 mm diameter, Cat. No.: 110656, GE Life Sciences). The filter was placed onto a microscope slide and 10 uL of antifade mountant (Molecular ProbesTM SlowFadeTM Diamond Antifade Mountant, Cat. No.: S36963, Invitrogen) added before the coverslip. On an inverted fluorescence microscope (Leica DM16000B), cells were counted in 10 locations for each filter. Three to five replicates were made for each sample and the resultant counts averaged.
